'''Herbert Eric Huppert''' (born 26 November 1943<ref name=whoswho/>) is an Australian-born and educated [[geophysicist]] resident in [[Cambridge]], United Kingdom.  He was Professor of Theoretical Geophysics and Foundation Director, [[Institute of Theoretical Geophysics]], at the [[University of Cambridge]], from 1989 to 2011, and a Fellow of [[King's College, Cambridge]], from 1970 to 2025.<ref>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303180636/http://www.itg.cam.ac.uk/people/heh/|archivedate=3 March 2016|url=http://www.itg.cam.ac.uk/people/heh/|publisher=University of Cambridge|location=Cambridge|title=Herbert Huppert ScD FRS}}</ref>

==Education and early life==
Huppert was born in Sydney and he received his early education at [[Sydney Boys High School]] (1956–59).<ref name=whoswho/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.shsobu.org.au/wp-content/uploads/professors.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=10 April 2016 |url-status=live |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160302191432/http://www.shsobu.org.au/wp-content/uploads/professors.pdf |archivedate=2 March 2016 }}</ref> He graduated in [[applied mathematics]] from [[Sydney University]] with first class Honours, a University medal and the Barker Travelling Fellowship in 1964. He then completed a PhD supervised by [[John W. Miles]] at the [[University of California, San Diego]],<ref name=mathgene>{{MathGenealogy|id=50418|name=Herbert Eric Huppert}}</ref><ref name=phd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Herbert Eric|last=Huppert |title=Excitation of lee waves in a stratified flow by semi-elliptical obstacles |publisher=University of California, San Diego |year=1968 |oclc=707177465|id={{ProQuest|302333519}}}}</ref> and came as an ICI [[postdoctoral research|Post-doctoral Fellow]] to [[DAMTP]] in [[Cambridge]] in 1968.{{fact|date=May 2022}}

==Career and research==
He has published using fluid-mechanical principles in applications to the [[Earth sciences]]: in [[meteorology]], [[oceanography]] and geology. He was a member of the Editorial Board of the Journal of Fluid Mechanics (1970–1992), the [[Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society]] (series A) (1994–99), The Proceedings of the Royal Society (series A) (2015-2020) and Geomechanics and Geophysics for Geo-energy and Georesources (2014 — ) and has been on the Council of the [[Royal Society]] (2001–03). He was Chairman of a [[Royal Society]] Working Group on [[bioterrorism]], which produced a Report entitled 'Making the UK Safer', on 21 April 2004. He was also chair of the European Academies Science Advisory Committee (EASAC) Working Group that produced a report for the European Parliament and President on [[carbon capture and storage]]. He was awarded the 2011 Bakerian lecture for his research into geological [[fluid dynamics]]. Since 1990 he has held a part-time Professorship at the University of New South Wales in Sydney, Australia.

===Awards and honours===
Huppert was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1987|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1987]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|author=Anon|year=1987|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/herbert-huppert-11670/|publisher=royalsociety.org|location=London|title=Professor Herbert Huppert FRS|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117015649/https://royalsociety.org/people/herbert-huppert-11670/|archivedate=17 November 2015}}</ref> In 2005 he was the only non-American recipient of a prize from the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]], being awarded the [[Arthur L. Day Prize and Lectureship]] for contributions to the [[Earth sciences]].{{citation needed|date=July 2016}} He has been elected a Fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]],{{when|date=July 2016}} the [[American Physical Society]]{{when|date=July 2016}} and the [[Academia Europaea]].{{when|date=July 2016}}. In 2020 he was awarded a Royal Medal and named Scientist of the Year in Earth Science. In 2024 he was elected to the Prof. N. R. Kamath chair professorship at IIT Bombay, Mumbai<ref>{{cite web |title=NR Kamath Distinguished Lectures: Unravelling Geophysics and Navigating Biotech Frontiers |url=https://acr.iitbombay.org/news/nr-kamath-distinguished-lectures-unravelling-geophysics-and-navigating-biotech-frontiers/ |website=Indian Institute of Technology Bombay}}</ref> and was the recipient of a Global Australian Award (Sustainability & Climate Change).<ref>{{cite web |title=2024 Global Australian Award Winners |url=https://globalaustralians.org/2024winners |website=globalaustralians.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2025 he was appointed to  a Westlake University (China) Distinguished Fellowship.<ref>{{cite web |title=news-M3_lab |url=https://m3.westlake.edu.cn/index/news.htm |website=m3.westlake.edu.cn}}</ref>  

==Personal life==
In 1966, Huppert married Felicia (née Ferster);<ref name=whoswho/> she was an Emerita Professor of Psychology and a past fellow of [[Darwin College, Cambridge]].<ref>Felicia Huppert's {{ORCID|0000-0003-2696-2286}}</ref> They divorced in 2016.<ref name="WW 22">{{cite web |title=Huppert, Prof. Herbert Eric, (born 26 Nov. 1943), Professor of Theoretical Geophysics and Foundation Director, Institute of Theoretical Geophysics, Cambridge University, 1989–2011, now Professor Emeritus; Leverhulme Emeritus Research Fellow, 2013–15; Fellow of King's College, Cambridge, since 1970; Dean of Science Professor, University of Bristol, since 2012; Professor, School of Mathematics and Statistics, University of New South Wales, since 2012 (Visiting Professor, 1991–96) |url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U21289 |website=[[Who's Who 2022]] |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=25 August 2022 |language=en |date=1 December 2021}}</ref> His sons, Julian and Rowan, studied at [[the University of Cambridge]]. [[Julian Huppert]] was the Liberal Democrat Member of Parliament for Cambridge from 2010 to 2015 and is now the Foundation Director of the Intellectual Forum of [[Jesus College, Cambridge]]. 

== Controversies==

In 2025 Kings College stripped him of his fellowship due to sexual harassment allegations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lambert |first=Sean O'Neill |date=2026-05-17 |title=King’s College Cambridge professor excluded over sexual harassment claims |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/education/article/cambridge-kings-college-professor-herbert-huppert-fellowship-0x25n72l2 |access-date=2026-05-18 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=King’s excludes fellow over sexual harassment allegations |url=https://www.varsity.co.uk/news/31724 |website=Varsity Online |language=en}}</ref>
